plan:
EXPERIMENT DESIGN — "Does ZB-2p achieve a near-zero bubble rate in practice when profiled on multiple GPUs?"
(Design-only document. No experiment has been run; /workspace contains no code, and all source-specific claims below are marked as either brief-confirmed or literature/context-based.)

════════════════════════════════════════════
1. OBJECTIVE AND HYPOTHESIS
════════════════════════════════════════════
Objective: Empirically determine whether the ZB-2p schedule (automatic planner output of the zero-bubble pipeline-parallelism Megatron-LM fork), activated via --zero-bubble-max-pending-backward = 2 × (number of pipeline stages), achieves a near-zero pipeline bubble rate on real multi-GPU hardware, and — if it deviates — localize the cause.

Hypothesis H1 (from the Zero Bubble Pipeline Parallelism paper): ZB-2p reduces theoretical bubble to ~0, while 1F1B retains (p−1)/(m+p−1) and ZB-1p retains roughly (p−1)/(m+p−1) minus ~75% of it. Operational predictions:
  P1: measured ZB-2p steady-state bubble rate ≤ 1–2% absolute (per scheme's own idle share of iteration time);
  P2: measured ZB-2p bubble rate < ZB-1p < 1F1B (ordering test);
  P3: deviations of ZB-2p from its planner's predicted timeline are attributable to identifiable causes (comm wait, stage imbalance, synchronization skew), not to the scheduler itself failing.

════════════════════════════════════════════
2. CONFIGURATION MATRIX
════════════════════════════════════════════
Factor matrix (all arms run at identical model size, microbatch count m, global batch, and total GPU count per configuration):

  Scheme (3): 1F1B | ZB-1p | ZB-2p
  Pipeline size PP (2): 4 | 8
  Placement (2): single-node (≤8 GPUs, NVLink) | multi-node (e.g., 2 nodes × 4–8 GPUs, Ethernet/IB inter-node)
  Stress scenarios (2, run for ZB-2p only unless resources allow all arms):
    S1 stage-load imbalance: one stage's compute inflated ~20% (e.g., wider MLP) to see if ZB-2p's slack absorbs or leaks bubbles;
    S2 high inter-node latency: place PP=8 across 2 nodes so T_comm/T_iter is elevated.

Core matrix: 3 schemes × 2 PP sizes × 2 placements = 12 cells.
Stress extensions: 2 scenarios × ZB-2p × {PP=4, PP=8} × 2 placements = up to 8 cells.
Repeats: ≥3 per cell → 12 × 3 = 36 core runs + 8–24 stress runs ≈ 44–60 runs total. Each run: 5 warmup iterations (excluded) + 50 measured steady-state iterations (single-node) or 30 (multi-node, slower).

Node split rationale: PP=4 and single-node PP=8 are single-node cells; PP=8 multi-node and all S2 cells are the multi-node subset (~1/3 of core cells) — this isolates the inter-node stress axis without doubling the whole matrix.

════════════════════════════════════════════
3. ACTIVATION OF ZB-2p (brief-confirmed flag semantics)
════════════════════════════════════════════
--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward set to 2 × PP (e.g., PP=4 → 8; PP=8 → 16). Per the paper/fork context, this pushes the schedule into the ZB-2p regime (two backward chunks in flight per stage); the fork's automatic planner then emits the schedule. Verification at runtime: assert from the fork's log/planner output that the emitted schedule is labeled ZB-2p (the fork prints the schedule type); do not infer mode from the flag value alone. Memory note (context-based): ZB-2p holds more activations; if OOM occurs, enable optimizer sharding / reduce microbatch and record this as a deviation in the run log rather than silently changing the model size between arms.

════════════════════════════════════════════
4. CONTROLS AND BASELINES
════════════════════════════════════════════
  C1 (primary baseline): 1F1B — textbook bubble rate predicted analytically as (p−1)/(m+p−1) for each (m, p) pair.
  C2 (attribution control): ZB-1p — separates "zero-bubble machinery exists" from "2p scheduling specifically drives bubble to zero."
  C3 (measurement-validity control / sanity check): the 1F1B baseline's measured steady-state bubble rate must match (p−1)/(m+p−1) within a pre-set tolerance (e.g., ±20% relative or ±2 percentage points absolute). If it does not, the profiling methodology itself is suspect and all results are quarantined until the cause (timer overhead, window placement, sync skew) is fixed. This check is run first, before any ZB arm.
  C4 (planner cross-check): for every ZB-2p run, extract the planner's predicted timeline and compare with the measured timeline.

════════════════════════════════════════════
5. MEASUREMENT METHODOLOGY
════════════════════════════════════════════
Metric definition (primary): bubble_rate = Σ_r idle_r / (p × T_iter), where idle_r is time rank r is neither computing a forward/backward chunk nor doing overlapping communication within its schedule slot, and T_iter is the steady-state iteration time. Reported per scheme and per configuration as BOTH absolute (idle share of iteration time, %) and relative to the 1F1B baseline of the same cell.

Measurement window: strictly steady-state. First 5 iterations discarded as fill/warmup; last 2 iterations before ramp-down (drain) excluded; fill/drain phases are reported separately (as their own overhead figure) but never folded into the steady-state bubble rate, since fill/drain inflates all schemes equally in kind but unequally in magnitude and would confound the near-zero claim. If the fork's timeline tool marks fill/drain boundaries, use them; otherwise detect steady state as iterations with stable T_iter (drift < 1% over a 10-iteration window) and cut the window conservatively inside it.

Instruments (dual, as agreed):
  (a) Megatron per-rank timers (forward/backward/comm/optimization elapsed times per rank per iteration) — primary, low overhead;
  (b) torch.profiler (or equivalent trace export) on all pipeline ranks for a 5–10 iteration window in a subset of runs — independent cross-check of idle windows; used in at least one run per core cell.
  (c) The fork's clock-profile/timeline visualization (context-based: the zero-bubble repo ships a timeline dump) for direct schedule-vs-measured comparison.

Timeline-vs-measured mismatch analysis (turns the number into a diagnosis):
  A "mismatch" = an idle window present in the measured per-rank timeline but absent in the planner's predicted schedule (i.e., the rank should have had work). Mismatch rate reported as fraction of predicted-busy time lost. Localization protocol:
    - window coincides with cross-rank communication wait → classify comm wait (verify via NCCL/torch.distributed timeline markers);
    - window follows an upstream stage's slow chunk → classify load imbalance (correlate with per-stage chunk durations);
    - window varies across repeats with no systematic schedule position → classify synchronization skew / jitter (report variance across repeats);
  Each ZB-2p run receives a mismatch taxonomy so the final claim reads "near-zero, and residual bubbles come from X," not just a percentage.

Run hygiene: lock clocks if permitted, pin ranks, record NCCL version, GPU model, driver, and the emitted schedule; identical seeds/data across arms within a cell; inter-run cooldown to rule out thermal drift; per-iteration timers logged to disk for offline recomputation.

════════════════════════════════════════════
6. ANALYSIS PLAN
════════════════════════════════════════════
  A1: per cell, mean ± std of absolute bubble rate across ≥3 repeats; report 95% CI (t-based, small n acknowledged).
  A2: ordering test P2 via pairwise comparisons (Wilcoxon signed-rank across matched cells, or bootstrap CI on scheme differences; n is small — nonparametric preferred over ANOVA).
  A3: near-zero test P1: absolute bubble rate ≤ 2% (pre-registered threshold) per ZB-2p cell; report every cell, including failures.
  A4: planner fidelity: per ZB-2p cell, predicted vs measured timeline divergence (mismatch rate + taxonomy from §5).
  A5: stress analysis: ZB-2p bubble rate delta between balanced vs S1/S2 cells; determines whether near-zero survives real-world stressors.
  A6: C3 sanity gate reported first; all downstream numbers conditional on it passing.

════════════════════════════════════════════
7. SUCCESS / FAILURE CRITERIA
════════════════════════════════════════════
  CONFIRMED: ZB-2p shows absolute steady-state bubble rate ≤ 2% in all balanced core cells (single- and multi-node), with 95% CI upper bound < 5%, ordering P2 holds, and residual idle is taxonomized as comm/imbalance/skew with mismatch rate ≤ ~5% of predicted-busy time.
  PARTIALLY CONFIRMED: near-zero holds in single-node balanced cells but degrades measurably under imbalance or multi-node comm — then the answer is conditional and the taxonomy identifies which stressor breaks it.
  NOT CONFIRMED: ZB-2p bubble rate materially exceeds threshold in balanced cells, or planner-predicted schedule and measured timeline diverge beyond mismatch tolerance, or C3 sanity gate fails (methodology invalid; redesign measurement before concluding anything about ZB-2p).

════════════════════════════════════════════
8. FEASIBILITY ASSESSMENT
════════════════════════════════════════════
  Hardware: minimum 8 GPUs of one type for single-node cells; 2 nodes × 4–8 GPUs for multi-node cells. GPU-disabled here — execution assumed to happen on an external stand (stated assumption).
  Memory: ZB-2p's higher activation footprint is an explicit resource constraint: budget a model configuration sized for the ZB-2p worst case; if OOM forces optimizer sharding, apply it identically across all three arms in that configuration and log it.
  Runtime: ~44–60 runs × (55–85 iterations) ≈ a few hours of GPU wall time per configuration class; well within a one-day allocation per node-pair. Feasible.
  Software: Megatron-LM fork with zero-bubble support; NCCL; torch.profiler. Network disabled in this sandbox — repo acquisition must occur on the execution stand.

════════════════════════════════════════════
9. ASSUMPTIONS (vs. fixed requirements)
════════════════════════════════════════════
Fixed by task: design-only; ZB-2p activated via zero-bubble config flag (brief); no execution claimed.
Assumed (not confirmed by local code): external multi-GPU stand availability; specific Megatron fork version matching the zero-bubble paper's code; availability of timeline dump utility; GPU clock control permissions; that compute dominates comm for the chosen model in single-node cells (needed for clean baseline sanity check).

════════════════════════════════════════════
10. UNCERTAINTIES (open, resolved only by execution)
════════════════════════════════════════════
  U1: Flag semantics --zero-bubble-max-pending-backward = 2×PP are brief-confirmed, not code-confirmed; runtime schedule-type verification (§3) is the safeguard.
  U2: ZB-2p memory pressure may constrain model size or require optimizer sharding; its effect on the comparison must be neutralized across arms.
  U3: Whether a built-in bubble-rate metric exists in the fork is unknown; the dual-instrument methodology does not depend on it.
  U4: Magnitude of residual bubbles under imbalance/inter-node comm — the central empirical question; taxonomy in §5 is designed to answer "why" even if the answer is "no."
  U5: Small repeat count (n=3) limits statistical power; conclusions rest on effect size plus planner-fidelity analysis, not solely on significance tests.
